A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adjoint Matching work and contain readable main text and complete Appendices A–G. Tables, figures, algorithms, and derivations can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original one-dimensional simulations and text-to-image fine-tuning experiments, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and generated samples in Section 7 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds training-progress results for ImageReward, control cost, and ClipScore in Appendix A, Figure 6.

M1.justification: The memoryless noise schedule, Adjoint Matching objective, lean adjoint equations, and both fine-tuning algorithms are unchanged. The revised proof does not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same one-dimensional example and text-to-image task using licensed image-text data. The new training curves remain within this coverage; inverse-problem applications appear only in related work.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain the base model, DRaFT-1, DRaFT-40, DPO, ReFL, and continuous and discrete adjoint methods. Figure 6 uses existing comparators; newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 Figure 6 introduces evaluation over training wall-clock time using separate test datasets of size 200, including control-cost measurements. The existing 1,000-prompt evaluations, training budgets, and appendix ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 examines how reward, control cost, and text-image consistency evolve during optimization. Existing analyses of reward weighting, guidance, optimizer settings, noise schedules, and sampling steps are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors across three fine-tuning runs with independently sampled prompt sets. Figure 6 extends this same reporting convention to new curves; no increased run count or changed statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 6 adds training trajectories, showing DRaFT-1's higher late-training reward and control cost alongside Adjoint Matching's stronger late-training ClipScore. All existing table values are retained: for example, Table 2 still reports ClipScore 31.65 ± 0.19 for Adjoint Matching with lambda = 12500 and noiseless sampling.

T1.justification: Appendix E.3 replaces Proposition 7's conditional-expectation ODE argument with an integral-equation argument using conditional expectations. It also adds Proposition 8 and a Gronwall-based uniqueness proof. This substantially revises the mathematical support for the algorithm's central critical-point guarantee, while retaining its statement.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the SOC formulation, memoryless fine-tuning requirement, Adjoint Matching algorithm, and claimed consistency, preference, and diversity advantages.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 removes the categorical assertion that the omitted terms have nonzero variance and that basic/continuous adjoint gradients remain nonvanishing at the optimum. The more qualified discussion of potentially better convergence and lower variance remains.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains the same optimizer settings, 40 timesteps, batch size, two 80GB A100 GPUs, noise offsets, timestep subsampling, clipping rules, and metric libraries. Existing runtime information is relocated without new implementation or resource-access disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands research positioning through a new conditional-sampling discussion, relating inverse problems to reward fine-tuning through r(x) = log p(y|x) and discussing Denker, Wu, and Du's approaches. It also adds prior DDIM formulations, quadratic-reward guarantees, GFlowNet alignment, and further diffusion-sampling work.

P1.justification: There are localized grammar, terminology, and cross-reference edits, an expanded related-work section, and a rewritten proof subsection. The title, overall section organization, and main explanatory narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the three-panel Figure 6 and rearranges existing displays, including moving v1 Table 8 to v3 Table 4. Existing sample images and the tradeoff plot are retained; appendix figures and tables are renumbered and reflowed.

improvement.justification: The new optimization diagnostics and fuller related-work discussion improve empirical transparency and context. Appendix E.3 makes the central proof more explicit, but new Proposition 8 switches from the controlled drift in Eq. (216) to the base drift in Eq. (217), leaving a gap as written. This limits the theoretical gain. With the method and existing experimental results unchanged, the supported overall improvement is modest.
